questions.question: How does green_set create a token watermark in the toy?
options: It hashes the previous K=4 tokens and marks half the vocabulary green according to the hash parity
It signs the whole output with a private key
It appends an HTML comment to the prompt
It inserts a visible logo after decoding
questions.explanation: green_set hashes the last four token IDs and includes token t when (t+h) % 2 == 0. watermarked_sample then chooses the green half with probability bias=0.9.

questions.question: What statistic does detect(tokens) report?
options: The fraction of tokens that are in the prompt vocabulary
A z-score comparing observed green tokens with the 50% expected count after the K-token prefix
The exact number of paraphrases in the sample
The C2PA certificate chain length
questions.explanation: detect counts green membership from index K onward, sets expected=n*0.5 and std=sqrt(n*0.5*0.5), and returns (green_count-expected)/std. A threshold such as z>=4 is evidence, not a provenance proof.

questions.question: Why does paraphrase weaken the toy watermark?
options: Paraphrase increases the watermark bias to 1.0
The detector ignores every token after the first four
Replacing token IDs changes the hash contexts and can turn green choices into red choices for the detector
Paraphrase attaches a new C2PA signature automatically
questions.explanation: The watermark is statistical and context-dependent. paraphrase replaces a fraction of the sequence, disrupting both the token choices and the rolling hash contexts used to reconstruct green membership.

questions.question: What does Stable Signature do differently from C2PA metadata?
options: It puts a visible corner label on every image
It signs a provenance manifest without changing the image generator
It only watermarks text tokens
It fine-tunes a latent-diffusion decoder so generated images carry a fixed latent message detectable after generation
questions.explanation: Stable Signature embeds a learned signal in the image generation process, while C2PA records a signed provenance assertion. They protect different channels and fail under different transformations.

questions.question: Why are C2PA metadata and a watermark complementary?
options: Metadata can carry a rich signed chain but be stripped; a watermark can persist through some transforms but carries only a small signal
They are interchangeable names for the same private key
A watermark automatically authenticates every image without a signer
C2PA metadata survives every edit by definition
questions.explanation: C2PA is an authenticated provenance record whose metadata may be removed. A watermark is embedded in content and can survive compression, but it is model-specific and not a complete chain of custody.

questions.question: Why does a missing SynthID signal not prove human origin?
options: The detector only works on images
Content from models that never applied SynthID, or content transformed enough to erase it, is also unmarked
SynthID always gives a positive score on human text
A missing signal proves the C2PA signer was trusted
questions.explanation: Absence is compatible with many non-human sources and with paraphrase or other transformations. Watermark detection can support a positive provenance claim for participating systems, not certify every unmarked item as human.
